option.label: UPPER glume 1.6–2.7 mm long
option.detail: Identify the second outer glume and measure its body. Gould gives1.6–2.7mm; Diggs gives1.5–2.7mm. Do not measure the lower glume, whole spikelet or a hair.

option.label: LOWER lemma lateral nerves not roughened
option.detail: Inspect the lateral nerves of the lower floret lemma with magnification. Gould says not scabrous here; Diggs calls these nerves smooth. This does not prove the whole lemma is hairless, shiny or smooth, or that the glumes are smooth.

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Inspect the LOWER lemma’s lateral nerves
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould says these lateral nerves are not scabrous. Diggs confirms smooth nerves, contrasting rough lateral nerves in D.sanguinalis. Magnification is needed.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: A smooth nerve is not proof that the whole lemma, its margins or the outer glumes are hairless. Vegetative traits alone do not reliably separate these crabgrasses.

diggs.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O’Kennon (1999), Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
diggs.confirmation: Exact key: leaf blades glabrous/sparsely pubescent; lower lemma lateral nerves smooth; spikelets2.8–3.6mm; second glume1.5–2.7mm. Key path has winged flowering branches and light brown/grayish fertile lemma at maturity. Genus supplies membranous ligule, two florets and minute/absent first glume.
diggs.citation_history: Existing records label exact key1263; preserve originals. Genus starts1263; named key/account is on1264, before footer DIGITARIA/POACEAE1264.

hill_country.retained: Flat5–10mm blades, whitish undulate margins, open sheath, variable hairs, erose0.5–2.5mm membrane and rooted decumbent culms. No reliable vegetative separation from D.sanguinalis. No true-stolon inference.
